chapterTitle: Chapter 3: Synaptic Memoriam of a steel fossil shell
editorText:
A large belly of fog slept over a large opening in the valley alluding the others to strange figures scattered in a mangle mass of steel and snow, from that tall glooming tower like pebbles from a fallen meteor, the carapaces spread deeper into the valley as far as the eye could see. John was silent with no remark to Tau’s comment, but his silence spoke for him. He kneeled down in the fog, wafting it away to reveal the cold carapace of what seemed like an ancient machine. The vast shells of the disposed sentient had a disorienting effect. Tao and Shai had never seen a site less akin to that of a Mongolian grave yet never of such a scale, such destruction.

“It’s like they all collectively came here, to die”. Tau’s voice was a mix of confusion, and sorrow. “There’s hardly anything left of this one?” Tex knelt down, splaying his fingers out to grasp one of the shells. “Wait” Shai tried to stop Tex in the action, but was unsuccessful. Tex ripped from the carapace one of its mangled arms. “I don’t think they just came here, and died. They’ve taken a hell of a beating.”, “We don’t know how long these things have even been here. I’ve never seen anything like it” Shai was reluctant to believe that such a mass of what felt like harmless machines could have sustained intentionally the damage that Tex was implying, She wanted to believe something unintentional and inconsequentially had fallen upon them. But Tex had other views, his tone spoke of something sinister at play, riddled with concern.

“Kitten what would it take to plug me into it’s neural network is it possible with these things. I mean they must have a memory core. Could we.. somehow see what they saw in their final moments?”, “Certainly captain, I can possibly reroute some of your nanobots to repair any weathered or damaged circuitry within it’s memory glands . When you connected to the facility I was able to extract the latest build archives so I have a reference to go off”. Tex intervene between the two. “I think it’s circuits should be mostly preserved, there are bodies still up on these mountains preserved like they fell yesterday from pre-war time. The cold has a funny way of keeping the dead alive”, Tex looked over to John. “Ok let’s give it a shot, I’m going to tether to it”. Tex looked over to Shai but said nothing almost as though he was concerned but to what John and Tau could not quite put their finger on. They didn’t make much of it anyway.

John knelt down, placing his hand gently over one of the machine's frame. The skull, or what John had assumed to be it’s skull emitted a soft bio luminescent glow which kissed the inner edges of an aesthetically streamlined hardened frame protecting a gelatinous substance within.

John reached in through the frame touching what felt like hard glass through the suit’s kinetic touch sensors. It seemed he almost intuitively knew where to touch as the others looked on, slightly anxious. Nothing could be seen on the surface of the glass, no recesses, no insignia, just a soft glow. A soft hiss let out as streams of mist bellowed out from a small pressure port at the necking of the machines brain like transparent dome. Beneath a series of wires like a pine cone extruding from a core, resembled a machine like brain which almost took the shape of a humans. It wasn't a circular dome as such but elongated, holding deceivingly from the front, more mass than that of a human skull.

John extended his robotic arm out to the machine, his palm softly laying over the machines brain. “The battery in this thing is dead to the core.. You can’t exactly pick up any life signs or data packets. I mean it’s hard to read these things. The memory is magnetic like the older ones. it requires a boot but i don’t want to fry the synapses. Tau can you give me an analysis on the inputs and outputs from the current flow. How much juice do I have to give this thing before I turn this brain and those memories to Mush.” “Sure John, Aaah you can’t do that with your new body, no IC for that kind of analysis huh?”, “Umm it’s great at analysis and tapping into systems however it needs a live feed to interpret anything. On the dead level lets just say i’m skin and steel and can’t do much. If something is dead I’ll still need your skills to ah test the waters.”

“Sure boss no worries,  Beginning analysis now” Kitten beamed from John’s suit an impressive 3d diagram of the sentient being. Overlaying the entire biology of the machine.

From it’s neural network to it’s auxiliary systems and even the heating cores within it’s sensors and actuators at the finger tips. The chart listed the biology of the being in Amperage draw with a colour variable soft amber blue. Any organic life illuminated in green. Kitten hummed softly flying the 3 dimensional projected view to focus in closer on what appeared to be a cerebellum just above the beings neck although protruding more slightly outwards than it’s human counterparts “Ladada da da daaa”..

Kitten seemed lost in a network, humming in melodic harmony. She felt herself flying through the synapses as her sandpit projected the scanned workings of it’s network she felt herself flying through a sea, of fanning dark to light amberous blue tendons. She could see a light glow floating in what seemed like an ocean. Transparent the fluid was thin enough to allow gaseous diffusion and metabolic consumption. It was pristine, comforting and enabling of life. It coexisted in what seemed like a perfect organism “Hmmm interesting”, hummed Kitten. . Then her melodies stopped, pausing abruptly gone like that in a sea of memories

“John, there is more going on here that I can comprehend, I may need to ask Shai’s opinion on this one, I mean she is the fairest biologist even as a medic than I.” Kitten was firm in her collection. John looked over to Shai nodding in approval giving a firm distinct tilt on his forehead in her direction.

“Tapping in now Sir” Shai was pleasant in her response with the enthusiasm of a 16 year old girl walking into her first greenhouse. Although the greenhouse she found herself in was far more than she could have ever imagined. She felt her mind slip into the beauty of the synapsial tree like structures. “Captain this entire brain, it was grown almost with a direct input it seems of someone from the past, the memory is formed like rings in the stems of each synapsial trunk ring”

Her eyes now veered into the distance of the generated virtual scan kitten had processed. “The genetic printing has naturally imbued plant photosynthesis as a survival mechanism. This explains the biology of the stem roots”. Tau intervened with Shai’s explanation humbly yet concisely. “It’s a regulated nervous system you are looking at Shai”..Shai paused then responded kindly. “Of course Tau, I have already generated the neural tree” Shai passed a data packet in Tau and Tex’s Visors. “Here take a look for yourself”

“You aren’t wrong, but it’s not just a voltage regulator. It also creates sugar and oxygen from carbon dioxide, water and sunlight. It’s a full organic ecosystem of sorts, and the bacteria. They are well man made.. Wow, I don’t think you realise what we have stumbled on here John. It’s a self preservation system. The metabolised oxygen from the photosynthesis preserves the brain”

“What the fuck. How is that even possible” Tex gracefully interrupted with his usual masculinity.

“Photosynthesis to keep the neural memory cores alive, it’s a an engineered survivability trait”. John spoke as though he had just collectively synced with Shai’s explanation.

“Genetic engineering and the correct fluids one might imagine!” Shai fearlessly and confidently concluded.

“John…” uttered Kitten softly, she seemed concerned, not distressed but cautious “We won’t be able to disconnect you straight away if something happens.. There’s a power down process, This is an incredibly sensitive grown network they have created..” Shai gave John a moment to comprehend what she had just explained.

“You’ll need to actuate a power down process from within the  mental bank. You can’t just sever the connection instantaneously, or you could create unforeseen neural surges and fry the memory fibres of the print”, “Fuck…” said John. “You’ll.. be dead, well not dead dead. but.. Brain dead”

“Well.. fuck” said John. Kitten was quick to regain the teams confidence. “I can Que auditory sounds through your interface as markers if we need you to get out, something familiar. You will still have residual sound of your surroundings in the real world, however it’s easy to get lost and think they are part of your emergence in the machines memories”.

“How do you know so much of this Kitten, from such little time” said John.

“Archives John, the doctor left many notes from his research, I’ve been studying the human machine network interface problems from the data pool since we stopped last night to refuel”,

“Ok, ok aaaah.. can you audio Que a gong.” , “Like a temple gong?, “Interesting choice there Cap!” said Shai looking confused. “Yes of the Buddhist kind Idk it makes sense, machines and this whole facility, doesn’t really seem like the kind of place you would find a temple gong does it!”, “Good point, but captain, this is Nepal” Shai spoke cheerfully, crossing her arms resting her finger on her chin in an aha moment. “Is there anything else I should know about Kitten”. John turned his head looking to the others as he waited for the AI to compute her response patiently unbothered more contemplating if he was coming out of this alive.

“Yes captain, your suit.. it will be completely dead when you are connected. Your autonomous systems will remain online. but when you are tethered, no Somatics. To avoid electrical and signal fluctuations, you’ll be in a cage essentially, your somatic signals are rerouted to the conscious realm in an almost sleep like state” said Kitten.

“Ok so I will be dead to the world, my suit will be dead to the world as well.. lucky I have a team of trained armoured orbital protectant Equalisers, a medic and an AI to watch over me, right?”. Tex chuckled slightly at Walker's positive outlook despite all the wet towels that had just slapped him in the face. “Can i connect outside the suit and leave it in sentry mode?”, “Well technically you could.. but i wouldn’t recommend it, you’d be more vulnerable, the suit acts as a Faraday cage preventing electrical fluctuations or possible EMP insertions from completely severing the bridge… I just thought you should know if something does happen, we will be down the firepower”. John drew a deep breath, “I’m sure it will be fine Kitten”“OK enough chit chat. I’m going in”.

As John connected with the dormant circuits, the ghostly echoes of a fallen machine's memories reverberated in his consciousness ever so slightly, but not at once.
